question_text: Calculate the eutectoid temperature and composition for a 4140 steel, containing $0.40 \% \mathrm{C}, 0.83 \% \mathrm{Mn}, 0.30 \% \mathrm{Si}, 1.0 \% \mathrm{Ni}$, and $0.20 \% \mathrm{Mo}$. For plain carbon steel, the eutectoid temperature is approximately $723^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and the eutectoid composition is $0.77 \% \mathrm{C}$. The approximate change in eutectoid temperature ( ${ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ) per $1 \mathrm{wt} \%$ of alloying element is: Mn: $-15, \mathrm{Si}:+25, \mathrm{Ni}:-14, \mathrm{Mo}:+92$. The approximate change in eutectoid composition (\% C) per 1 wt\% of alloying element is: Mn: -0.054, Si: -0.108, Ni: -0.03, Mo: -0.337. Give your answer as a tuple: (eutectoid_temperature, eutectoid_composition)The units of each required answer are (C, %), respectively.
